paragraphs.source_en: Avoiding the other women and pretending nothing was amiss, Lady Sena rode home in her palanquin through the slanting evening sunlight.

units.source_en: Avoiding the other women and pretending nothing was amiss, Lady Sena rode home in her palanquin through the slanting evening sunlight.
units.source_zh: 濑名姬避开其他女人，佯装无事，踏着斜阳坐轿回去了。

paragraphs.source_en: Motoyasu truly was still alive! The knowledge brought Lady Sena immense relief, as though the world before her had suddenly filled with light; but then the opposite possibility occurred to her: what would she do if Motoyasu had died in battle?

paragraphs.source_en: If she had the child openly and honorably inherit the Matsudaira estate, might she herself gain even greater power? Lady Sena felt no guilt over such absurd fantasies. What expression would Motoyasu wear if, in their bedchamber after their long separation, she told him of it?

paragraphs.source_en: When the palanquin stopped at the steps of her residence, Usui, wife of Sakai Saemon-no-jō Tadatsugu, was the first to come out and greet her. “You came home so late that I was truly worried.”

paragraphs.source_en: Motoyasu’s aunt Usui closely resembled her mother, Lady Kayōin, and was a beautiful woman with a long face. Lady Sena did not much care for her. There was no real reason for it, but she always felt that Usui was watching her every moment, and she simply could not bring herself to like her.

paragraphs.source_en: Lady Sena’s expression changed at once. Turning to Usui, she said, “You should be more careful with your words. Lord Imagawa is my uncle.” With that, she strode straight toward the children’s room without looking back.

paragraphs.source_en: Inside, Takechiyo sat on the floor, his eyes fixed on the folded paper in Okame’s hands. The sister and brother looked so adorable that maternal affection welled up in Lady Sena’s heart.

paragraphs.source_en: Okame certainly resembled Ujizane, though there should have been nothing remarkable in that, since both Ujizane and Otsuru were related by blood to the Imagawa family. But that was not how Lady Sena saw it now. She could think only one thing: was this child Ujizane’s?

paragraphs.source_en: It is said that only a mother can know for certain who fathered her child. Yet, ironically, even Lady Sena did not know who Okame’s father truly was. Ujizane had brutally violated her on the day before her wedding, and the next day Lady Sena had become Motoyasu’s wife. If this child was Ujizane’s daughter, Lady Sena would be utterly disgraced. One was Ujizane’s child and the other Motoyasu’s—then whose children was Lady Sena truly meant to bear?
